This rating is mainly because of Dr. Simon Bramley Towl. I've been on their Wellness Plan for 2 pets. More than a year ago, my dog was diagnosed with early renal failure. He's been on a prescription diet.  Early in July, he began not eating much & losing weight. I brought him in and they did blood tests. Dr. Towl came to talk to me. He pointed out all the tests that were very abnormally high. He then said I should think about euthanasia sooner not later. He repeated several times "think about in weeks not months". He also stressed that even if my dog died, I'd be responsible for the balance for tests done. He offered NOTHING to do to help him eat, etc. I'm not sure how he treated my dog behind doors but he didn't even touch him in my presence. He seems to be able to read reports well but any other Vet skills are completely lacking. I took my dog to another Vet who gave me supplements, subcutaneous fluids to administer and now almost 2 months later, he is eating, gained a few pounds, has his same energy, loves walks, etc. I will not return with either of my pets and advise no one to see Dr. Towl.

I’ve given Banfield on Oregon Ave in South Philly several chances, but the repeated lack of urgency, poor communication, and constant scheduling issues have left me deeply frustrated and disappointed.

When my puppy was about six months old, I discovered a lump on his neck and immediately contacted Banfield, clearly expressing my concern. Despite the urgency, the earliest appointment they could offer was five days later. There was no guidance, no concern—just a cold, dismissive response. As a first-time pet owner, I felt lost and unsupported. Ultimately, my pup ended up scratching it, and it abscessed.  I had to take my pup to an emergency vet to have the lump drained, which was both expensive and possibly avoidable with more timely care or direction. It's incredibly frustrating to pay a substantial monthly fee for the Optimum Wellness Plan, only to be unable to use it when it matters most.

More recently, they prescribed allergy medication for my dog but never followed up to check on how he was responding. They claimed to have called the day after the appointment to follow up —when he hadn’t even started the medication yet. I had to reach out myself as his medication was running out, only to be scheduled for a follow-up appointment a week later. When I showed up for the appointment, they told me there was no appointment in their system. Very frustrating!!

Some members of the front desk staff have been consistently disorganized and unprofessional. As a new pet owner trying to do right by my dog, it’s disheartening to feel brushed off and unsupported when all I want is reliable care and clear communication.

Update: I received a call from this location to hear my concerns, and I truly appreciate them going the extra mile to make things right. That effort spoke volumes to me and showed a genuine commitment to customer care.

they almost killed my dog.

my american bully has been acting strange for a week, not eating as much, fatigued and with no energy. yesterday we took her over here so they could check her out. we told the doctor her symptoms, they were 8 hours with my dog. they took a blood sample to see if they could find anything wrong with her. nothing showed up. the doctor told us to wait 8 days with the vomit and diarrhea medication and if she wasn’t getting better to come back to have an x-ray. we pushed for the x-ray to be done that same day and still told us to wait. later that day she’s at home and she’s secreting this red pus from her privates and we get increasingly worried. today, we took called banfield in the morning to make an appointment for today, the doctor wanted us to wait until the afternoon to check her when we PUSHED that it was an emergency. when it was around the time we called again, a secretary asked us how our dog was, we told her the symptoms and she referred us to an “emergency hospital”. turns out they DONT DO EMERGENCY SURGERIES and banfield knows this and they still referred us there. we finally go to an actual emergency vet clinic and they checked her out, told us she has an infection in her uterus and that if we waited any longer to bring her in she would’ve died. banfield made us waste our time, waste 300 dollars on medications that were for the symptoms NOT the root of the problem. my dog is currently in surgery, and i just keep remembering our banfield doctor saying “i have a bad feeling that something is wrong with her, but im going to hold off on the x ray.” a uterus infection isn’t going to show up on a blood test. it only shows through an x ray or ultra sound. shame on this hospital. they did not do their job as veterinary professionals and rule everything serious out right then and there, instead they gave up and just went with the easy “solution” which was treating the symptoms.
